A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DPRNet research, with readable text, equations, tables, and figures. v2 includes Appendices A–E; the supplied v1 ends with references despite mentioning supplementary material. Newly supplied details are distinguished from demonstrated changes to the underlying work.

before.justification: v1 reports original tone-mapping experiments, component and loss ablations, cross-dataset evaluations, and a 25-participant user study.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark and user-study results, with additional LUT sensitivity, high-frequency reconstruction, and training-dataset comparisons in the main text and appendix.

M1.justification: The four-component framework and four loss categories remain. However, Section 3.5 revises IDE from predicting a mask that multiplies high-frequency features to predicting an additive residual directly (v1 Equations 1–2 versus v2 Equations 10–11). This is a localized computational change; the expanded GTP/LTT descriptions do not independently establish further procedural changes.

E1.justification: The main coverage remains HDR+, HDRI Haven, HDR Survey, and UVTM. Appendix E newly reports unsuccessful evaluation on MIT FiveK, although without scores or a detailed protocol. Calling HDRI Haven a new benchmark does not establish additional coverage relative to v1, which already uses that collection.

E2.justification: v2 adds CODEFormer and RECNet to the HDR+/HDRI Haven comparisons and ZS-Diffusion to generalization comparisons. Table 11 also adds LPTN to the HDR Survey comparison. CSRNet's UVTM comparison disappears, while its HDR Survey result remains in Table 11. These changes broaden the evaluated comparator families substantially.

E3.justification: The reported 2.9M-parameter model and 818K Tiny variant are replaced by a 212K model. New protocols compare HDR+ versus HDRI Haven training and evaluate Laplacian-extracted high-frequency maps using PSNR-HF, SSIM-HF, and Canny-based EPI. Main dataset splits and the 25-user, 50-image study design remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds LUT-size and grid-count sensitivity studies, quantitative high-frequency analysis, and training-dataset generalization ablations. The pyramid-depth study moves from v1 Table 3 to v2 Appendix B.1, with revised results. Conversely, the direct Gaussian/Laplacian pyramid replacement comparisons and numerical joint removal of GTP/LTT disappear, although the latter remains illustrated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Both provide user-study ranking counts and percentages; changed counts do not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Results are extensively replaced and supplemented. For the differently sized model, 4K HDR+ PSNR changes from 27.90 to 27.71 and HDRI Haven from 27.89 to 28.30; these are not controlled same-configuration gains. UVTM TMQI changes from 0.9364 to 0.9540. New CODEFormer results exceed DPRNet in 480p SSIM and LPIPS. Ablation results change, and user-study first/second-place counts change from 423/562 to 413/576.

T1.justification: The IDE reconstruction recurrence is substantively revised, replacing the explicit high-frequency-times-mask term with a predicted residual. Appendix A also supplies explicit multiscale reconstruction and high-frequency loss definitions. No theorem, proof, or formal stability guarantee is added; most other new equations formalize existing descriptions.

C1.justification: v2 adds introducing HDRI Haven as an explicit benchmark contribution, whereas v1 presents it as an existing public benchmark. The core DPRNet claims remain, but headline 4K PSNR margins change from 2.58/3.31 dB to 2.39/3.01 dB. The HDRI Haven margin now compares against newly added RECNet rather than CoTF.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new training-dataset comparisons as evidence that HDRI Haven supports better generalization and discusses LUT/grid choices as quality–efficiency tradeoffs. Appendix E adds substantive applicability limits, attributing FiveK failures to noise affecting high-frequency extraction, problematic reference images, and inconsistent reference adjustments. v1 contains no corresponding limitations discussion.

D1.justification: v2 specifies local descriptors of dimension 6, a 4-by-4 patch grid, LUT discretization of 9, conditional modulation, pyramid supervision targets, and the VGG19 perceptual-loss feature. It adds a brief HDRI ground-truth construction description and changes the demo address. Conversely, v1's batch sizes, explicit input/output bit depths and color spaces, and example resizing dimensions are omitted.

R1.justification: v2 expands positioning around unsupervised and zero-shot diffusion methods, real-time and semi-supervised mapping, and hardware constraints. It adds substantive discussion and citations including ZS-Diffusion, newer LUT approaches, and Difference-of-Gaussian applications, while removing several older references. HDRI Haven is also repositioned from an existing evaluation resource to a claimed benchmark contribution.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, motivation, method descriptions, and experimental discussion are extensively rewritten. Global/local mapping gains explicit subsections and equations; generalization and user-study sections exchange order; pyramid-depth analysis moves into a structured appendix. These changes substantially alter the narrative beyond the addition of scientific content.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. Figure 1 replaces parameter–performance scatterplots with four-dataset bar charts, Figure 3 is redrawn, and ablation tables are reorganized. Numerous qualitative panels are added, while some existing examples are retained or relocated, including the landscape comparison moved into Figure 14.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency through explicit loss and LUT specifications, and strengthens assessment through newer baselines, high-frequency measurements, and training-dataset comparisons. The FiveK discussion usefully qualifies applicability. These benefits are tempered by losing direct Gaussian/Laplacian pyramid controls and batch/input-format disclosures; loss weights and precise HDRI target-generation procedures also remain unspecified.
